skill.name: lifi-stablecoin-swap
skill.description: Build production 1:1 stablecoin swaps with LI.FI Intents, where the amount sent equals the amount received with no visible gas or solver fees, on the same chain or across chains. Use for guaranteed-output USDC or USDT transfers, enterprise or fintech transfer flows, integrator onboarding and Partner Portal setup, and the quote, approve, escrow-open, and status lifecycle. Covers the @lifi/intent TypeScript SDK as the primary path and order.li.fi REST endpoints as a language-agnostic alternative. For classic swaps and bridges, Composer, Earn, or the wider LI.FI product surface, use the lifi skill.
skill.summary: Guide LI.FI Intents integrations for fixed-output, same-chain and cross-chain stablecoin transfers.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: All 87 static matches are false positives: Markdown backticks, fixed LI.FI URLs, relative imports, documented environment configuration, and chain constants were misclassified as dangerous operations. One conditional medium-risk issue remains because the quickstart exposes an integrator key through a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable; its permissions must be verified before client-side use.

remediation.issue: Potential client-side exposure of the LI.FI integrator key.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the key is designed for public browser use and cannot authorize sensitive actions or incur unbounded charges. Otherwise keep it server-side and proxy quote requests.

remediation.issue: The quickstart uses NEXT_PUBLIC_LIFI_INTEGRATOR_KEY without stating its permission boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Document whether the key is public, which scopes it has, and how operators rotate or restrict it.

remediation.issue: Examples perform asset approvals and escrow opens.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit pre-transaction validation for supported chain, token address, quote expiry, minimum received amount, and displayed user confirmation.

semantic_findings.description: The quickstart configures NEXT_PUBLIC_LIFI_INTEGRATOR_KEY, which exposes its value in a browser build. If this key carries authorization, billing, or configuration privileges, third parties could reuse it.

content.user_title: Build 1:1 stablecoin swaps with LI.FI Intents
content.value_statement: Stablecoin transfer flows need predictable received amounts across supported chains. This skill guides LI.FI Intents quotes, approvals, escrow opening, and order tracking for fixed-output transfers.
actual_capabilities: Explains LI.FI Intents setup and integrator onboarding requirements.
Builds quote requests with the @lifi/intent TypeScript SDK.
Describes ERC-20 allowance checks and approval transactions.
Guides escrow order construction and open transaction submission.
Shows order-status polling through the LI.FI API.
Documents REST API concepts for non-TypeScript integrations.
limitations: Requires a LI.FI-enabled integrator and supported route.
Does not guarantee a quote remains valid after its expiry time.
Does not replace wallet, contract, or production security review.
Does not cover classic LI.FI swaps, bridges, Composer, or Earn.

use_cases.title: Add fixed-output transfers to a fintech app
use_cases.description: Build a guided USDC or USDT transfer flow with quotes, approvals, escrow opening, and order updates.

use_cases.title: Prototype a cross-chain payment experience
use_cases.description: Use the SDK lifecycle to test supported stablecoin transfer routes before production integration.

use_cases.title: Plan a partner integration
use_cases.description: Review onboarding, key handling, API lifecycle, and operational checks for a LI.FI Intents implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Start with a transfer plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to plan a LI.FI Intents USDC transfer from Base to a supported destination. List prerequisites and user confirmations.

prompt_templates.title: Request a stablecoin quote
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to request a LI.FI Intents quote for 100 USDC. Explain each required input and how to validate quote expiry.

prompt_templates.title: Build approval and escrow flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a TypeScript flow that checks allowance, waits for approval confirmation, validates wallet chain, and opens a LI.FI Intents escrow order.

prompt_templates.title: Review production safeguards
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this LI.FI Intents transfer design for quote validation, minimum received amount, key exposure, transaction confirmation, and order-status error handling.

output_examples.input: Plan a 100 USDC transfer from Base to another supported chain.
output: Prerequisites: enabled integrator, supported route, connected wallet, and verified token addresses.
Flow: request quote, verify amount and expiry, confirm with user, approve token, wait for receipt, open escrow, then track status.

output_examples.input: What should happen before opening an escrow order?
output: Validate wallet is on source chain.
Check quote remains valid and meets minimum received amount.
Confirm allowance transaction succeeded before submitting escrow transaction.

output_examples.input: How should an app show order progress?
output_examples.output: Show pending, delivered, settled, expired, and failed states. Include transaction links and a clear refund path for expired orders.

best_practices: Validate source chain, token addresses, quote expiry, and minimum received amount before every transaction.
Wait for approval confirmation before opening escrow, and display every signing action to the user.
Treat integrator keys as sensitive until LI.FI documents their public-use permissions and limits.
anti_patterns: Do not promise a 1:1 outcome without comparing quote input and output in matching token units.
Do not submit an escrow order after an unconfirmed approval transaction.
Do not place privileged or billable keys in client-side environment variables.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers LI.FI Intents stablecoin quotes, approvals, escrow orders, and order tracking.

faq.question: Does it guarantee every transfer is 1:1?
faq.answer: No. Verify each current quote, route availability, token decimals, and received amount before user confirmation.

faq.question: Can I use it for cross-chain transfers?
faq.answer: Yes, when LI.FI supports the selected route and your integrator is enabled for it.

faq.question: Do I need an integrator key?
faq.answer: The documented SDK and API flows use an onboarded LI.FI integrator key.

faq.question: Should I expose the integrator key in a browser app?
faq.answer: Only if LI.FI confirms it is public and safely restricted. Use a server-side proxy for privileged keys.

faq.question: Does this skill replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. Review wallet interactions, contract addresses, quote validation, and key handling before production release.
